4034.name: Christian McCaffrey
4034.adp_commentary: Market drafts him ~RB5 (ADP 5.7) while the board values him ~RB9. You're paying up for ceiling against an age-30, Achilles-history availability cap. A slight reach at cost in a format where RB-adjacent value is available later.

availability.history: 2024 lost 13 games to bilateral Achilles tendinitis (soft-tissue, both legs) + late PCL sprain; answered with a 17-game RB1 season in 2025. Age 30 + Achilles history is the recurrence/decline risk, not a current injury.

brief.prose: San Francisco entered the season with a stated plan to trim McCaffrey's touches after he led the NFL with 413 last year, and Week 1 showed it wasn't just talk: third-round rookie Kaelon Black out-carried him 14-10, with McCaffrey's 15 total touches (10 carries, 5 catches) edging Black's 14 (14 carries, 1 catch) by just one. Shanahan called the split deliberate afterward: 'I thought they both ran really hard and really well... that was the goal for us coming into this, trying to balance it out more, whether it was with Kaelon or getting Deebo some carries.' McCaffrey kept every catch on the day, so the passing-down role -- the highest-value share of this offense's touches -- is still his alone; what changed is the early-down carry math, where a rookie is now taking a real, coach-endorsed share rather than mop-up work. Whether a near-even carry split repeats in Week 2 or Week 1 leaned on game flow is the actual watch item.
brief.rationale: A coach-confirmed, deliberate carry split with a rookie (not an injury fill-in) is a real early-down role change a preseason bell-cow projection likely hasn't fully priced -- worth a human look, even though the receiving role (the highest-value piece) is unaffected.

5850.adp_commentary: RB at ~25.2. Top-12 RB talent, but a pending domestic-violence case (felony charge, undecided) plus a 2025 knee that sapped his second half make this a genuine avoid-until-clarity at cost. The ADP has not fully absorbed the legal risk.

brief.prose: The legal-outcome bet resolved into a confirmed absence, not a pending risk: the NFL placed Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List on Aug. 30, which bars him from practicing or playing in any capacity for as long as he's on it, three days after Brown County formally charged him with two misdemeanors (battery, criminal damage to property) tied to the May domestic incident. GM Brian Gutekunst has said a suspension could still follow once the NFL's own conduct review concludes, meaning the exempt-list stint may only be the front end of a longer absence rather than the whole of it, with no set timeline either way. Green Bay hedged the same day, trading a 2028 sixth-round pick for Steelers RB Kaleb Johnson to sit behind newly-elevated starter MarShawn Lloyd (5 of 7 snaps on Green Bay's preseason opening drive, plus a touchdown). Jacobs remains the clean zone-scheme fit in LaFleur/Stenavich's offense whenever he is eligible to return, but Lloyd, not Jacobs, is Green Bay's playable back for the foreseeable future.
brief.rationale: Confirmed Commissioner's-Exempt placement (not just a pending charge) makes this a real, current zero with no return timeline — a bigger and more certain role delta than the Aug. 28 brief priced in.

His earliest eligible return is Week 6 (Oct. 18 vs. NYJ), with Week 8 vs. Miami the more realistic target.
